findings.text: Make the icon set a real, exercised theme dimension. It is modeled as a per-theme treatment (manifest.treatments.iconSet: line|filled|pixel) but only 'line' is ever rendered — aquarelle is the sole registered theme — so the 'filled' (Phosphor fill) and 'pixel' (pixelarticons) columns of ICON_SETS are dead data that silently bit-rots.
findings.motivation: Icon family is modeled as a per-theme treatment (ThemeIcon resolves manifest.treatments.iconSet against ICON_SETS), implying themes were meant to vary it. In practice there is one registered theme (aquarelle=line) after commit 8fae18e purged the rest, so 'filled' and 'pixel' are never rendered. Dead branches drift: swapping the live 'line' set from Phosphor to Lucide (2026-07-11) left filled=ph:*-fill and pixel=pixelarticons:* untouched, so a future theme selecting 'filled' or 'pixel' would get a family inconsistent with 'line' and with each other, and no test guards this.
findings.behavior: Only 'line' is rendered (aquarelle is the sole theme). Since 2026-10-18 a guard test (tests/unit/themes/treatments.test.ts) keeps the filled/pixel columns coherent (one icon family per column, all three per entry, no reused ids); the direction (a theme using filled/pixel vs. collapsing to line) is OWNER Q6.
findings.approach: Decide product intent: (a) icon family becomes a themed/selectable dimension — add at least one theme that uses filled or pixel (or expose it in settings) so all three columns are exercised, plus a test asserting each ICON_SETS entry defines all three coherently; or (b) drop the multi-set abstraction — collapse ICON_SETS to the single active family and remove IconSetName, simplifying ThemeIcon. (a) is the 'make it part of a theme' direction requested here.
findings.success_signal: Either every IconSetName column is rendered by some registered theme (guarded by a test), or the unused columns are removed and ThemeIcon no longer branches on a set that never varies.

findings.text: Invite-modal picker cannot re-invite a contact who is already invited but hasn't accepted — they show as disabled 'already in group' with no path to resend
findings.motivation: Originally locked product decision (epic invite-group-member-from-contacts, DD-4) wanted a pending-but-not-yet-joined contact to stay selectable so an admin could resend a lost/expired invite. Live e2e testing proved this can't work as specced: group.memberPubkeys updates the moment inviteByNpub succeeds (an MLS commit), not when the invitee accepts, so the picker's already-member check can't currently tell 'invited, still pending' apart from 'fully joined'.
findings.behavior: Today: after A invites B, B's picker option becomes disabled ('already in group') and stays that way until B accepts or the invite is otherwise resolved (e.g. cancelled). There is no way to resend via the picker while pending.
findings.approach: The 'invitation pending' label half is done (2026-10-18, admin-and-invite-guards: invite_pending disabled reason, en 'invitation pending' / de 'Einladung ausstehend'). Remaining: the resend action — OWNER question 3 in bug-reports/LOOP-HANDOFF-2026-10-17.md (cancel + re-invite in one tap recommended if DD-4 stands).
findings.success_signal: Re-opening the invite picker for a group where a contact was invited but hasn't accepted shows that contact as selectable (not disabled), and resubmitting the invite succeeds.

findings.text: If a leaver's kind-13 departure signal fails to send, they purge locally but persist as a normal roster entry forever, with no pending-cleanup state and nothing for an admin to finalise
findings.motivation: This is a silent, unrecoverable divergence between a member's real state (gone) and every remaining member's roster (present, indistinguishable from an active member). Unlike the normal ghost window it never resolves and shows no pending indicator, so remaining members are misled indefinitely. Surfaced while writing docs/behavior/group-administration.md.
findings.behavior: leaveGroupImpl catches a failed kind-13 send and proceeds with the local purge (soft-leave). When the send fails (e.g. the leaver is offline), no departure signal ever reaches the group: no admin can finalise the removal and no leave-pending/removal-pending state is shown. The out-of-band-leave spec covers the ghost window assuming the signal was sent, but not the send-failed case.
findings.approach: Record the behaviour and decide whether to mitigate (retry/queue the kind-13 until sent, or surface a local indicator) or accept it as a documented risk in the out-of-band-leave spec.

findings.text: External-signer users (NIP-07/NIP-46) get no automatic relay backup: BackupProvider only schedules backups when a local private key exists
findings.motivation: A user signed in through a browser extension or remote signer believes their groups are backed up like everyone else's, but nothing is ever published; losing the device loses all group state. The limit is now documented in docs/behavior/backup-and-recovery.md §3, but not fixed.
findings.behavior: Corrected 2026-10-18: in NIP-07/NIP-46 mode the stored local key stays loaded, so BackupProvider kept scheduling backups with it (and connectNdk rebound NDK to the local key). Now gated on isLocalMode (shouldScheduleBackups); Settings shows 'Automatic backup is off while an external signer is connected.' Whether external-signer users get a manual or signer-routed backup is OWNER Q5.
findings.approach: Handle with the signer-authority work (2026-09-26 review task R04): route backup encrypt/sign through the active signer, decide whether background NIP-44 encrypt/sign prompts are acceptable for NIP-46/NIP-07, and gate the restore flow accordingly.

findings.text: Multi-tab MLS group cache coherence: each tab caches its own group instances, and a write in one tab leaves another tab at a stale epoch (single active client or cross-tab invalidation needed)
findings.motivation: Each tab builds its own MarmotClient and caches group instances from groups.loadAll(); no BroadcastChannel/leader election exists (only navigator.locks in welcomeSubscription.ts join lock). A write in tab B (commit, leave, or the destroy→re-join in joinIdempotent) leaves tab A's instance stale; A can pass groups.has + loadGroup checks using B's overlay while sending/subscribing with stale state and re-persisting it over B's. Surfaced by a Codex HIGH on bug invite-accept-not-atomic-across-page-unload round 1; waived there by the Decider (pre-existing class, epic-sized).
findings.behavior: Two tabs on the same identity; accept (or any epoch-advancing action) in one, then act in the other → the second tab sends undecryptable messages / overwrites fresher MLS state; today's outcome is silent divergence. Related write-back gap (leave purge, 2026-10-15): after a leave's groups.destroy, a still-cached instance (another tab, an in-flight handler, or a departure send that outlived the 5 s timeout) can save the MLS state again, leaving an orphan without tombstone — excluded from backups and purged on re-accept, but not swept.
findings.approach: Choose (a) one active client per origin via navigator.locks leader election, passive tabs render from IDB and forward actions, or (b) BroadcastChannel mls-state-changed {groupId} after every group.save/destroy with receivers evicting and reloading; (a) is simpler to reason about. Add a two-context e2e that advances the epoch in tab 1 and sends from tab 2.
findings.success_signal: The two-tab e2e passes and no stale-epoch sends are logged; withGroupJoinLock becomes the only cross-tab primitive or is subsumed by the election

findings.text: Poll receipt clock is not ordered across concurrently active tabs, and vote-seq uniqueness without Web Locks is in-tab only
findings.motivation: Decider (Fable) waiver/follow-up from bug run poll-residual-ordering-and-close-retry (2026-10-16). Belongs to the multi-tab-mls-cache-coherence design.
findings.behavior: Per-tab in-memory receipt counters are not ordered across tabs and the lease get-max-set is serialised only in-tab (a tab can regress the persisted mark); allocateVoteSeq is cross-tab unique only where navigator.locks exists.
findings.approach: Resolve under multi-tab-mls-cache-coherence: shared lock around the lease write, or a single-writer tab.
findings.success_signal: Two-instance unit test with shared IDB orders receipts and seqs across instances without Web Locks

findings.text: Forwarded signed envelopes (profiles today) lack ADR-012's epoch/freshness bound and a persistent one-shot set
findings.motivation: ADR-012 requires forwarded meta-events to be epoch/freshness-bounded and one-shot by inner event id; any future forwardable kind would inherit the gap. Low impact today because profile merges are last-writer-wins.
findings.behavior: envelopeVerifier.ts checks only shape, kind, signature and an optional g tag; one-shot is an in-memory per-subscription Set (~:185-194) reset on reload; no producer emits the g tag (profiles exempt). Verified 2026-10-18.
findings.approach: Add a created_at freshness window (or join-generation bound) and persist the seen-inner-id set per group (idb, bounded); emit the g tag if a group-scoped forwardable kind is added.

findings.text: A stale-group replace in one tab does not tear down the same group's MarmotGroup/EpochResolver in other open tabs; their late save can overwrite the freshly joined state
findings.motivation: Found by the code-reviewer in stale-welcome-reinvite round 2. The join lock is cross-tab but teardown is per tab; the leave/destroy path has the same exposure. Narrow window (an evicted tab mostly buffers unreadable events without saving).
findings.behavior: Tab B keeps the old MarmotGroup for the group; its grace-timer save or an in-flight ingest can write the evicted MLS state back after tab A replaced it.
findings.approach: Post a crossTab store-changed notice for the group after a replace/destroy so other tabs dispose and re-subscribe it; ties to OWNER Q4 (single active tab).

findings.text: A stale-group replace bumps subscriptionGeneration, re-running the subscription effect for every group (full historical refetch for all)
findings.motivation: Correct but costly for users in many groups; noted by the code-reviewer in stale-welcome-reinvite round 2.
findings.behavior: Every replace attempt (including failed ones) tears down and rebuilds all group subscriptions.
findings.approach: Drop only the replaced group's entry from groupSubsRef and subscribe the missing groups without tearing down the others.

findings.text: DM composer Enter press hangs 30s under full-suite load in groups-dm-reactions
findings.motivation: Second sighting of an undiagnosed renderer stall that turns the full e2e gate red without a product signal; each red gate costs a 65-min rerun on the 1-CPU VM.
findings.behavior: In gate full-backup-react (2026-10-18) AC-60 timed out on locator.press('Enter') for 30 s while the composer was visible with text, the thread having just loaded the previous test's history (same keys, same relay). The spec passed 5/5 in isolation; the first sighting was AC-46 (comment in sendDmViaComposer). Same stall as a click: dm-pairing-pending-confirmation.spec.ts:214 timed out 30 s in 'performing click action' on chat-send-btn in gates full-pollpurge (2026-10-17) and full-dmswitch (2026-10-18) while the message had already reached the peer.
findings.approach: Capture an in-page long-task/performance trace around the thread-open history load under CPU throttling to find the main-thread blocker; consider a per-test relay wipe or unique keys between DM reaction tests.
findings.success_signal: Three consecutive full gates without a composer key-press timeout.

findings.text: Invite of a fresh peer fails with 'has not set up their Few identity yet' on the cold first relay test
findings.motivation: Second sighting on the 1-CPU VM (2026-10-18, gate full-signer: dm-block-contact :146, first test of the relay bucket); it fails the setup step and skips the spec's 4 serial tests, turning a 65-min gate red.
findings.behavior: createGroupAndInvite waits 60 s for invite-success; Alice's invite instead shows 'This user has not set up their Few identity yet', i.e. Bob's KeyPackage was not found on the relay when Alice fetched it. Only seen on the first relay test (cold next dev compile, fresh relay).
findings.approach: Check whether the invitee's KeyPackage publish has completed before the inviter fetches (helper readiness wait on the invitee's published KeyPackage), and whether the app's KeyPackage fetch retries once on an empty result; decide between a test readiness gate and a product retry.
findings.success_signal: Three consecutive full gates without the 'not set up their Few identity' setup failure.

findings.text: Replace does not await onMembersChanged and the onHistorySynced profile send, which can commit or persist on a destroyed group
findings.motivation: Code-reviewer finding (severity 6, inference, not reproduced) on stale-replace-retired-setup-untracked: work started from inside subscribeToGroupMessages that neither whenIdle nor the dispatcher drain covers can outlive a stale-Welcome replace's teardown.
findings.behavior: EpochResolver fires onMembersChanged without awaiting it (epochResolver.ts:292-295). Its body awaits persistGroup/reloadGroups and then runs void mlsGroup.commit() with no isCurrentGroup() re-check, so after a replace destroys and rejoins it can commit on the old MarmotGroup object (MLS state save + publish) and persist a stale overlay record. The onHistorySynced profile send checks isCurrentGroup only before sendRumorSafe, and the in-flight send is untracked.
findings.approach: Track the onMembersChanged and profile-send promises per group in pendingDrainRef (trackPending) or chain them into the resolver idle; re-check isCurrentGroup() immediately before mlsGroup.commit() and persistGroup.
findings.success_signal: Unit test: a replace started while an onMembersChanged body is suspended waits for it (or that body does not commit/persist once the group was replaced).

findings.text: Deleting a DM image while it is still uploading does not stick
findings.motivation: The delete action is offered on an uploading image, but the delete targets its temporary id, so the image comes back when the upload finishes and the peer receives a delete for an id that never exists; the behaviour doc now states this limitation.
findings.behavior: handleDeleteMessage publishes and buffers a delete for the random temp id; sendImageMessage then re-adds the final row under the event id and persistOwnSend stores it untombstoned, since nothing maps the temp-id signal to the event id.
findings.approach: Either hide delete/edit actions on temp-id (uploading) rows, or, after the upload, check the pending registry's hidden flag and issue the delete against the event id instead of re-adding the row.
findings.success_signal: Deleting an uploading image keeps it deleted after the upload finishes and after reopening the conversation.

findings.text: Pending-contact confirm badge reads 1 instead of 2 when the second held DM arrives late
findings.motivation: Intermittent red in the pairing spec (1 of 5 isolated runs, 2026-10-18) without a known product cause; either a test race or a held DM that is not counted when it lands around the confirm.
findings.behavior: The test waits until A's lastSeenAt for B advances (proof of at least one processed event), then confirms; after confirm the nav badge polled 15 s stayed at 1 instead of 2. B showed both messages.
findings.approach: Check whether a held DM arriving during or just after confirm is counted; if it is, make the test wait for both held events (e.g. poll the stored held count) before confirming.
findings.success_signal: The spec passes 10 consecutive isolated runs.

archive.text: ContactChat.tsx uses the same fetch-then-live-sub anti-pattern fixed in welcomeSubscription.ts: Phase-1 runs three parallel fetchEventsWithTimeout calls for DM history then Phase-2 opens three live ndk.subscribe calls, leaving a gap where events are silently lost.
archive.reason: The welcomeSubscription since-anchor fix does NOT transfer: ContactChat's primary DM path is kind-1059 gift-wraps whose outer created_at is randomized/backdated up to 2 days (NIP-59 privacy), so a since:fetchStartedAt filter on the gift-wrap live sub would DROP incoming DMs — a regression. since is only safe on the legacy kind-4 subs (real timestamps), whose inbound-only gap is negligible. Existing per-id dedup (ingestEvent/knownMessageIds + shouldIngestRumor) already absorbs the small overlap. Closing the gap properly would need a relay-replay mechanism that doesn't key on the spoofed gift-wrap timestamp — out of scope for a smell-driven refactor.

archive.text: A live leave whose identity capture failed falls back to the current leaf but does not write it onto the journal row, so a replay after a failed removal persist skips the removal
archive.reason: Unsound: a live capture can read a re-joined member's new leaf and bind it to an old leave rumor, so a replay would evict the re-joined member. Only an epoch-bound capture would make it sound, which live handling cannot obtain. Replay keeps skipping identity-less leaves (no eviction of a re-joined member outranks no lost removal). See bug-reports/journal-and-purge-followups-report.md.
